comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation classifies borrowings with an original maturity of less than one year as short-term borrowings. At December 31, 2024 and 2023, these consisted primarily of Federal Home Loan Bank advances totaling $12.7 billion and $13.2 billion, and commercial paper totaling $24.2 billion and $13.1 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC define short-term borrowings by the timing of maturity relative to the reporting date. GS defines unsecured short-term borrowings specifically as the portion of unsecured long-term borrowings maturing or redeemable within one year of the financial statement date. BAC defines short-term borrowings more broadly as any borrowings with an original maturity of less than one year, listing specific instruments like FHLB advances and commercial paper. While both address the classification of debt based on a one-year horizon, GS focuses on the reclassification from long-term to short-term for unsecured debt, whereas BAC focuses on the initial original maturity of diverse funding sources.

sentences.text: Unsecured short-term borrowings includes the portion of unsecured long-term borrowings maturing within one year of the financial statement date and unsecured long-term borrowings that are redeemable within one year of the financial statement date at the option of the holder.
The Corporation classifies borrowings with an original maturity of less than one year as short-term borrowings on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.

At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the majority of short-term borrowings consisted of Federal Home Loan Bank advances, which totaled $12.7 billion and $13.2 billion, and commercial paper, which totaled $24.2 billion and $13.1 billion.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair Value Option Election for Debt Liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has elected the fair value option for certain trading-related debt liabilities, classifying them as Long-term debt or Short-term borrowings on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C disclose accounting policies for specific subsets of their short-term borrowings involving fair value measurements. GS discloses that certain hybrid financial instruments classified as unsecured short-term borrowings are accounted for at fair value under the fair value option. Similarly, C discloses that it has elected the fair value option for certain trading-related debt liabilities, which are then classified as Short-term borrowings on the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Both filings indicate an overlap between short-term borrowing classification and fair value accounting for risk-managed positions.

sentences.text: Unsecured short-term borrowings includes the portion of unsecured long-term borrowings maturing within one year of the financial statement date and unsecured long-term borrowings that are redeemable within one year of the financial statement date at the option of the holder.
The Company has elected the fair value option for certain debt liabilities, because these exposures are considered to be trading-related positions and, therefore, are managed on a fair value basis.
These positions are classified as Long-term debt or Short-term borrowings on the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheet.
